constraints.field: NLP and graph theory (graph neural networks for text classification)

candidates.title: BoW wide MLP versus post-2022 text-graph models

evidence: Two surveys published in 2024 and 2025 show the area is active [@wang2024; @rizvi2025]
The baseline result it builds on appeared at ACL 2022 [@galke2022]
Novelty confidence is low, but a multi-seed replication of [@galke2022] has value by itself
https://github.com/lgalke/text-clf-baselines (licence MIT, last push 2026-04-21)
https://github.com/doGregor/TokenGraph responds (HTTP 200); its contents were not inspected
missing: Licence and completeness of the TokenGraph repository

evidence: Benchmark files are in the TextGCN repository data folder (URL responds, HTTP 200)
missing: Licence of the benchmark files is not stated by any API

evidence: An MLP on bag-of-words is light; token-graph models need pre-trained language model embeddings, which should fit 8 GB for short texts
missing: No hardware statement found for either codebase

evidence: Two existing codebases must be run under one protocol; no new model is needed
About 6 weeks: 2 for setup, 3 for runs over 5 seeds, 1 for analysis
The MLP codebase pins dependencies (requirements.txt, uv.lock); seeds must be added by the student
Accuracy on shared benchmarks with published numbers to compare against
Either outcome (MLP still competitive, or not) is reportable

candidates.title: Seed and graph-construction sensitivity of TextGCN

evidence: Evaluation sensitivity changed GNN rankings in node classification [@shchur2019]; relevance to text graphs is an inference
The challenge search did not reach closely related work, so it supports almost nothing
https://github.com/yao8839836/text_gcn exists; no licence; 112 open issues
Data and preparation scripts are in the same repository (build_graph.py, prepare_data.py)

missing: No hardware statement found; [@galke2022] notes the graph is O(N^2) in vocabulary plus corpus size, so memory on the larger benchmarks is unknown

evidence: One codebase; the study is a parameter sweep
About 5 weeks, dominated by environment setup for a 2018 codebase
No dependency file and no seed handling were found by the automated check of the repository
Accuracy mean and standard deviation over seeds and window sizes
A flat result is still reportable, but the legacy TensorFlow stack may not install

candidates.title: BoW MLP versus text graphs on low-resource languages

evidence: [@ghosh2022] states that existing work is mostly English-only
No close match was retrieved, but the dataset's own paper was not read and may report similar baselines
https://github.com/lgalke/text-clf-baselines (licence MIT)
https://huggingface.co/datasets/masakhane/masakhanews: licence afl-3.0, not gated, 31088 rows, about 96.3 MB to download, 96.4 MB in memory (dataset viewer figures)
Small corpora (a few thousand documents per language)
Graph models need tokenisation and graph construction for each new language; nothing is pre-built
About 8 weeks, which leaves no slack in an 8-week budget
Public data with fixed train/validation/test splits per language
Splits exist
missing: Which baselines the dataset paper already reports

evidence: Per-language preprocessing is the main risk
